response: Aspiration thrombectomy before primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is not associated with any benefit on clinical end points and might actually increase the risk of stroke. The concomitant administration of intravenous glycoprotein IIb/IIIa inhibitors and ischemic time do not seem to influence any potential benefits observed with aspiration thrombectomy. Therefore, aspiration thrombectomy is not considered beneficial for patients undergoing primary PCI.
